business.description: Hilton Metal Forging Limited is a forging company manufacturing forged products for railway, defence, energy, oil & gas, and industrial applications. The company has supplied over 2,500 railway wheels and has established capabilities in forged pipe fittings, railway wheels and wheel-set assemblies, and is evaluating opportunities in defence components and turbine components.

outlook.statement: The global manufacturing landscape is undergoing a structural transformation with increasing emphasis on supply-chain diversification, localisation, infrastructure development, energy security and strategic manufacturing capabilities, creating attractive opportunities for the forging industry.

Railway sector represents one of the most promising growth opportunities with significant investments in railway infrastructure, modernisation, freight corridors, high-speed and semi-high-speed rail networks, and replacement and expansion of rolling-stock fleets.
Defence sector presents strategically important opportunity with India's increasing focus on indigenisation and development of domestic defence manufacturing capabilities.
Energy sector transition towards reliable and efficient energy infrastructure creating substantial opportunities for forged turbine blades and other critical turbine components.

Global demand for forged pipe fittings supported by investments in energy infrastructure, replacement of ageing industrial assets, expansion of process industries and development of new manufacturing capacities.
Significant orders from customers based in the United States and Europe for supply of forged products, providing strong platform for strengthening export business.

Q1 FY 2026-27 shows encouraging evidence of transition with total revenue of approximately Rs 59.27 crore (vs Rs 22.43 crore in Q1 FY 2025-26, growth ~164%) and net profit of approximately Rs 1.81 crore (vs Rs 0.15 crore).

India metal forging market expected to grow from USD 5.08 billion in 2023 to USD 9.75 billion by 2030 at CAGR of 9.8%. Indian Railways plans to invest Rs 16,70,000 crore by 2031 and Rs 3,02,000 crore in 2025-26. Freight wagon market expected to nearly double by 2031 to Rs 25,000-30,000 crore. Railway sector revenue expected to grow 5% in FY26 with operating margins around 12%.

The deleveraging initiative is expected to support improved debt servicing capacity going forward. The strengthening of the Company's capital base and reduction in debt are expected to contribute positively to profitability in the coming periods.
